reconstruction.blind_decode: A taxi driver in Kyoto takes a woman passenger from in front of Kyoto University’s medical faculty toward Mizorogaike. He can see her during the drive, but when the taxi arrives she is gone and her seat is wet. He reports this to police; searching does not locate her or a related hit-and-run case. The account remains unexplained. A nearby unattended anatomy-department truck is presented only as an eerie coincidence, not an explanation. The named pond is real, while the detailed story is reconstructed from an unverified reprint of a newspaper item whose existence and headline are independently confirmed. A later version instead has a young woman board beside the pond on a rainy night.

probes.blind: Taxi driver and woman passenger; police are subsequent investigators.
The passenger undergoes the anomalous absence; the driver is observer and reporter.
A routine taxi trip toward Mizorogaike precedes the event, without a repeatable trigger rule.
No cause or agent is established.
The passenger is seen in transit but absent at arrival, with a wet seat trace.
The vehicle changes from containing the passenger to not containing her.
A single ordered episode runs from pickup through travel, disappearance, report, and search.
No taboo, rule, or reproducible condition is supplied.
Police investigation is post-event inquiry, not an evidenced preventive or control method.
The woman is not found and the matter has no resolved explanation.
Cause, identity/status of the passenger, and relation of the coincidence remain unknown.
The initial newspaper-connected form is distinct from a later rainy-night, pondside-pickup form.

reconstruction.reference_story: The initial form connected to the 1969 local Asahi article concerns a Kyoto taxi driver who takes a woman passenger toward Mizorogaike, observes her during travel, then finds her absent on arrival with a wet trace on the seat. Police search without locating the woman or a corresponding hit-and-run case. The reported correspondence between the pickup area and an unattended Kyoto University anatomy-department truck near the scene is not a causal explanation. Mizorogaike is a real pond. The newspaper item and headline are independently confirmed, but episode details depend on an uncollated mirror. The rainy, pondside-pickup version is a later variant and is excluded from the initial scope.
